scientific_question: Can hard-aligned metric learning improve native one-shot proposals when optimization starts exactly at M=1 and checkpoint selection uses held-out training hard score rather than the final epoch?

training.metric_initialization: fresh bounded log-residual metric M=exp(log(2)*tanh(r)); zero logits make epoch 0 exactly M=1 and keep M in [0.5,2]
training.checkpoint_selection: maximum held-out-training normalized hard-edge advantage over the identical unit trajectory; ties prefer the earlier epoch

validation.selection_normalizer: minimum input edge count, not released optimum
validation.pass_rule: positive three-seed mean learned-minus-unit normalized hard-edge advantage on every dataset
